2 wt.% Al is below 5 wt.% Al, so a single austenite phase prevails at room temperature; the RAP hot-rolled/water-quenched material is described as fully recrystallized with ~20 μm grains and retained Mn microsegregations.

overall_structure.value: Single-phase austenitic (γ) microstructure; hot rolling and water quenching produced a fully recrystallized microstructure with ~20 μm grain size and some retained Mn microsegregations.

unmapped_findings: For the Fe-30Mn-1.2C-2Al alloy (intermediate Al content in the 2–6 wt.% range), aging has a much smaller influence on tensile behavior compared with the Al-free alloy (weakening/embrittlement) and the 8 wt.% Al alloy (pronounced strengthening). [b0024, b0025]

The 2 wt.% Al variant does not show the pronounced j-carbide strengthening attributed to the ~8 wt.% Al variant; first results indicate nm-sized j-carbides can occur over a wide compositional existence range and are thermally very stable at 600 °C (100 h, modest coarsening), but this is discussed mainly for the high-Al variants. [b0025]

In Fig. 3c the total elongation drops to a minimum at 2Al, and in Fig. 3b the UTS passes through a minimum near 2Al (green 550 °C/24 h point annotated), indicating the 2Al alloy is a low-strength/low-ductility point within the Fe-30Mn-1.2C-xAl matrix. [figure_003]
No cracks, pores, or macrosegregations were observed in the final RAP materials. [b0021]
